title: A local map of complete Noetherian local rings has a flat Cohen presentation
statement: Let $\varphi:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings such that $A$ is $\mathfrak m_A$-adically complete and $B$ is $\mathfrak m_B$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then there are Noetherian complete local rings $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ and a commutative square of local homomorphisms $R\to S$, $R\twoheadrightarrow A$, $S\twoheadrightarrow B$, $A\to B$ in which the vertical maps are surjective and $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Write $f=\varphi:A\to B$, $\kappa_A=A/\mathfrak m_A$, $\kappa_B=B/\mathfrak m_B$. Since $f$ is local it induces a field homomorphism $\kappa_A\to\kappa_B$, so both residue fields have the same characteristic $p\ge0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-structure-power-series-surjection] to $B$ and to $A$ (Noetherian, so their maximal ideals are finitely generated, and complete): there are $m,n\ge0$, rings $\Lambda_B,\Lambda_A$, each a field of characteristic $0$ if $p=0$ and a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] if $p>0$, and surjective ring homomorphisms $v:S_0=\Lambda_B[[z_1,\ldots,z_m]]\to B$ and $q:R=\Lambda_A[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] (1), (3), (4): $R$ and $S_0$ are Noetherian local rings, complete for their maximal ideals, regular; $\mathfrak m_R=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ and $\dim R=n$ if $p=0$, $\mathfrak m_R=(p,x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ and $\dim R=n+1$ if $p>0$; likewise $\mathfrak m_{S_0}=(z_1,\ldots,z_m)$, resp. $(p,z_1,\ldots,z_m)$. A surjective ring homomorphism $h:(C,\mathfrak m_C)\to(D,\mathfrak m_D)$ of local rings is local and satisfies $h(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_D$: $C/h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)\cong D/\mathfrak m_D$ is a field, so $h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)$ is a maximal ideal, hence equals $\mathfrak m_C$; and an element of $\mathfrak m_D$ has only non-unit preimages, which lie in $\mathfrak m_C$. So $q$ and $v$ are local with $q(\mathfrak m_R)=\mathfrak m_A$ and $v(\mathfrak m_{S_0})=\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings, line 9769), first two sentences: choice of S -> B and R = Lambda[[x_1..x_n]] -> A by the Cohen structure theorem (Algebra, Theorem 032A)

proof.text: We lift $f\circ q:R\to B$ to a ring homomorphism $\phi:R\to S_0$ with $v\circ\phi=f\circ q$ and $\phi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S_0}$. Let $J=\ker v$ and $\bar v:S_0/J\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ the induced isomorphism. $J\neq S_0$ since $B\neq0$, so $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ ($t=1$ below). $J$ is closed for the $\mathfrak m_{S_0}$-adic topology: by Step 1, $v(\mathfrak m_{S_0}^k)=\mathfrak m_B^k$, so $v^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B^k)=J+\mathfrak m_{S_0}^k$ (if $v(s)=v(y)$ with $y\in\mathfrak m_{S_0}^k$ then $s-y\in J$), and $\bigcap_k(J+\mathfrak m_{S_0}^k)=v^{-1}(\bigcap_k\mathfrak m_B^k)=v^{-1}(0)=J$ because the complete ring $B$ has $\bigcap_k\mathfrak m_B^k=0$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $R_0=\mathbf Q$ if $p=0$ and $R_0=\mathbf Z$ if $p>0$. If $p=0$, every nonzero integer has nonzero image in $\kappa_B$, hence is a unit of the local ring $S_0$ (and of $A$, $B$, $R$), so these rings are $\mathbf Q$-algebras in a unique way and every ring homomorphism between them is $\mathbf Q$-linear; if $p>0$ every ring is a $\mathbf Z$-algebra and every ring homomorphism is $\mathbf Z$-linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-cohen-formally-smooth-adic], $R$ is formally smooth over $R_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_R$-adic topology. Let $g=\bar v^{-1}\circ f\circ q:R\to S_0/J$, an $R_0$-algebra homomorphism with $g(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\bar v^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=(\mathfrak m_{S_0}+J)/J$, since $f(q(\mathfrak m_R))\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$ ($q$, $f$ local) and $v(\mathfrak m_{S_0})=\mathfrak m_B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with $S=R$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_R$, target $S_0$ (complete for $I=\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ by Step 1), closed ideal $J$, $t=1$, $r=1$: it gives an $R_0$-algebra homomorphism $\phi:R\to S_0$ with $(S_0\to S_0/J)\circ\phi=g$, i.e. $v\circ\phi=f\circ q$, and $\phi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S_0}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings, line 9769): 'We lift the composition Lambda[[x_1..x_n]] -> A -> B to a map phi : R -> S ... formally smooth over Z in the m-adic topology (Lemma 07NL) by an application of Lemma 07NJ'

proof.text: Let $S=\Lambda_B[[y_1,\ldots,y_n,z_1,\ldots,z_m]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and regard $S_0$ as the subring of series involving only $z_1,\ldots,z_m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables] (with $i=n$) the map $\pi:S\to S_0$ that discards every term containing some $y_j$ is a surjective ring homomorphism which is the identity on $S_0$ and has kernel $(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$; put $v'=v\circ\pi:S\to B$, a surjective ring homomorphism with $v'(y_j)=0$ and $v'|_{S_0}=v$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] (1), (3), (4), $S$ is a Noetherian regular local ring, complete for $\mathfrak m_S$, with $\mathfrak m_S=(y_1,\ldots,y_n,z_1,\ldots,z_m)$ and $\dim S=n+m$ if $p=0$, $\mathfrak m_S=(p,y_1,\ldots,y_n,z_1,\ldots,z_m)$ and $\dim S=n+m+1$ if $p>0$; in particular $\mathfrak m_{S_0}S\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, as the generators of $\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ lie in $\mathfrak m_S$. Put $t_i=\phi(x_i)+y_i\in\mathfrak m_S$ (as $\phi(x_i)\in\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ by Step 2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to $\Lambda=\Lambda_A$, $T=S$, $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m_S$, $\alpha=\phi|_{\Lambda_A}:\Lambda_A\to S_0\subseteq S$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_n$: there is a ring homomorphism $\phi':R\to S$ with $\phi'(\lambda)=\phi(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda_A$ and $\phi'(x_i)=\phi(x_i)+y_i$. It is local: $\mathfrak m_R$ is generated by $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ (and $p$ if $p>0$), and $\phi'(x_i)=t_i\in\mathfrak m_S$, $\phi'(p)=p\in\mathfrak m_S$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings, line 9769): 'we replace phi by the map phi' : R = Lambda[[x_1..x_n]] -> S' = S[[y_1..y_n]] with phi'|_Lambda = phi|_Lambda and phi'(x_i) = phi(x_i) + y_i. We also replace S -> B by the map S' -> B which maps y_i to zero'

proof.text: The square commutes: $v'\circ\phi'=f\circ q$. Both are ring homomorphisms $R=\Lambda_A[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to B$. On $\lambda\in\Lambda_A$: $v'(\phi'(\lambda))=v(\pi(\phi(\lambda)))=v(\phi(\lambda))=f(q(\lambda))$ by Step 2, since $\phi(\lambda)\in S_0$ and $\pi$ is the identity on $S_0$. On $x_i$: $v'(\phi(x_i)+y_i)=v(\phi(x_i))+v(\pi(y_i))=f(q(x_i))+0$. Moreover $f(q(x_i))\in\mathfrak m_B$ since $q$ and $f$ are local, and $B$ is $\mathfrak m_B$-adically complete. By the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] (with $T=B$, $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m_B$, $\alpha=(f\circ q)|_{\Lambda_A}$, $t_i=f(q(x_i))$) the two homomorphisms are equal.

proof.text: $\phi':R\to S$ is flat. Suppose $p>0$ (for $p=0$ delete $p$ from every list below). The ideal $(p,t_1,\ldots,t_n,z_1,\ldots,z_m)$ of $S$ equals $\mathfrak m_S$: it is contained in $\mathfrak m_S$ by Step 3, and it contains $p$, the $z_j$, and $y_i=t_i-\phi(x_i)$, because $\phi(x_i)\in\mathfrak m_{S_0}=(p,z_1,\ldots,z_m)S_0\subseteq(p,z_1,\ldots,z_m)S$; so it contains the generators of $\mathfrak m_S$ of Step 3. These are $1+n+m=\dim S$ elements generating $\mathfrak m_S$ of the regular local ring $S$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] the sequence $p,t_1,\ldots,t_n,z_1,\ldots,z_m$ is a regular sequence in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Hence its initial segment $p,t_1,\ldots,t_n$ is a regular sequence: the nonzerodivisor conditions for its terms are those of the longer sequence, and $S/(p,t_1,\ldots,t_n)S\neq0$ since $(p,t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$. Now $R$ is a regular local ring of dimension $n+1$ whose maximal ideal is generated by $p,x_1,\ldots,x_n$ (Step 1), $\phi'$ is a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings (Step 3), and $\phi'(p),\phi'(x_1),\ldots,\phi'(x_n)=p,t_1,\ldots,t_n$ is a regular sequence in $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular], $\phi'$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 07NN, proof ('a regular system of parameters of R maps to part of a regular sequence in S'') and statement ('In particular R -> S is flat (see Algebra, Lemma 07DY lemma-flat-over-regular)'), with Algebra, Lemma 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM) for the regular sequence

proof.text: Conclusion: $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian local rings, complete for their maximal ideals (Steps 1 and 3); $q:R\to A$ and $v':S\to B$ are surjective local homomorphisms (Steps 1 and 3, and the remark of Step 1 on surjections of local rings), $\phi':R\to S$ is a flat (Step 5) local (Step 3) homomorphism, $f$ is local by hypothesis, and $v'\circ\phi'=f\circ q$ (Step 4). This is the assertion, with $S$ in the role of the statement's $S$.
